📰 General

Houthi Rebels Attack Cargo Ship in Red Sea, Kill Government Troops in Yemen •

Houthi rebels in Yemen launched an attack on a cargo ship in the Red Sea on Sunday, according to a report from the British military. The attack occurred off the coast of Yemen, a region embroiled in ongoing conflict. Simultaneously, the Houthi rebels also killed 16 government troops in a separate assault. This latest incident highlights the escalating maritime security concerns in the Red Sea due to the ongoing conflict.

🌍 World

Calla Walsh Attends Khamenei Funeral, Praises Him as Anti-Imperialist Icon •

Calla Walsh, a former prominent Democratic political figure, was present at the funeral for Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in Tehran on Saturday. She delivered a statement praising him as the “greatest anti-imperialist leader.” Walsh was observed wearing a hijab and traditional clothing during the event. The attendance of a Western political figure at the funeral highlights ongoing international engagement with the Iranian regime.

🦅 US

Farage Accused of Concealing Funds from Convicted Fraudster Ahead of Election •

A report alleges that Reform UK leader Nigel Farage received financial benefits from a convicted fraudster in 2023. The investigation, conducted by The Sunday Telegraph, suggests he accepted payments from the individual during the year prior to his election to Parliament. The report indicates a potential breach of parliamentary rules regarding the disclosure of these financial relationships. Reform UK has not yet responded to the allegations, and further investigation is reportedly underway.

💰 Business

Investment Firm Fired Cofounder Over Remote Work Policy Dispute •

William Nieporte, a cofounder of Bramshill Investments, has filed a lawsuit against the firm following his termination. The lawsuit alleges he was fired for violating a 2022 agreement requiring employees to return to the office in person. Nieporte and his co-managers had previously established this in-person work mandate with staff. The dispute centers around Nieporte’s continued remote work arrangement, which contradicted the signed agreement.

💻 Technology

Meccha Chameleon’s Viral Success Continues: 15 Million Copies Sold in 30 Days •

The indie game Meccha Chameleon has achieved remarkable sales success, surpassing 15 million copies sold within its first 30 days on the Steam store. This follows an initial 16-day period where the game sold 10 million copies. The game’s popularity stems from its unique hide-and-seek gameplay mechanic. The developer celebrated this significant milestone on the Steam store page.

🎭 Entertainment

Zendaya Dominates Met Gala, Showcasing Stunning Custom Valentino Gown •

Zendaya attended the 2024 Met Gala, held at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City. She wore a custom-designed white Valentino gown featuring a dramatic, sculpted silhouette and intricate embellishments. The gown was praised by fashion critics and social media users alike for its innovative design and Zendaya’s confident presentation. The actress posed for photographers throughout the evening, solidifying her status as a major fashion icon.

🏅 Sports

Brazil Faces Norway in 2026 World Cup Round of 16 – Odds & Predictions •

Brazil, currently ranked fifth, is set to play Norway in the 2026 World Cup Round of 16 on Sunday. The five-time World Cup champions are favored to advance, seeking a ninth consecutive quarter-final appearance. Current odds favor Brazil, reflecting their historical dominance and status as a top contender. The match will determine which team progresses to the next stage of the tournament.

🔬 Science

James Webb Telescope Detects Thick Water Ice Clouds on Distant Exoplanet •

The James Webb Space Telescope has identified substantial water ice clouds residing within the upper atmosphere of Epsilon Indi Ab, a planet resembling Jupiter located relatively close to our solar system. This discovery represents a significant finding regarding the composition of exoplanet atmospheres. Scientists emphasize that the results do not invalidate existing atmospheric models for gas giants. The observation provides valuable data for refining our understanding of planetary formation and evolution.

🩺 Health

Michigan Health Officials Investigate Spike in Cyclosporiasis Cases Following Fourth of July •

The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) is investigating a significant increase in cyclosporiasis cases across the state. As of Tuesday, over 572 cases have been reported, representing a more than threefold rise compared to the previous week. The outbreak appears to be linked to consumption of contaminated water, with investigations focusing on potential sources like recreational water. MDHHS is advising residents to take precautions, including thorough handwashing and avoiding untreated water sources, until the source of the contamination is identified.
